chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever bears oppression would not thank for blessings.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between bearing hardship and showing gratitude in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual correlation between *jafa'* (hardness of heart or inability to endure) and *shukr* (gratitude). Scholarly commentary suggests that those who lack the capacity to bear life's trials often fail to recognize the underlying wisdom in divine decrees, thereby diminishing their thankfulness for blessings. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) as a prerequisite for true appreciation of God's favors.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-37 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan that someone narrated that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Whoever bears oppression would not thank for blessings.”
